entry: [[France|French]] twin-engine, canard delta-wing multirole [[Fighter aircraft|fighter]] aircraft built by Dassault Aviation. Dassault markets it as an "omnirole" fighter able to perform several mission roles in a single sortie, including air supremacy, strike and nuclear deterrence. Disagreements over workshare in a joint European project, which became the [[Eurofighter Typhoon]], led France to pursue its own programme; a demonstrator first flew in July 1986. Introduced in 2001, the Rafale serves the French Air Force and Navy and has been selected by air forces including those of [[Croatia]], Egypt, India and the [[United Arab Emirates]]. It has seen combat over Afghanistan, Libya, Mali, Iraq and Syria.

Order of mostly Australian carnivorous [[Marsupial|marsupials]]. It contains four families: Myrmecobiidae, with a single living species, the numbat (*Myrmecobius fasciatus*); Thylacinidae, with the recently extinct [[Thylacine|thylacine]] (*Thylacinus cynocephalus*) and several fossil species; Dasyuridae, with 73 extant species, including quolls, dunnarts and the [[Tasmanian devil]]; and the extinct fossil family Malleodectidae, with six genera. Body sizes range from 4 grams in the long-tailed planigale, the smallest living marsupial, to 35 kilograms in the thylacine. Most species feed on vertebrates or [[Arthropod|arthropods]] such as insects. Their lower molars have a carnassial-like form, and each erupting molar works as a carnassial until the next pushes it forward in the jaw.

Process of inspecting, cleansing, transforming and modeling [[Data|raw facts and figures]] to discover useful [[Information|information]], inform conclusions and support decision-making. Varieties include descriptive statistics, exploratory data analysis, which seeks new features in data, and confirmatory data analysis, which tests existing hypotheses. Data mining emphasizes predictive modeling, business intelligence relies on aggregation, and text analytics extracts information from unstructured text. Data analysis is iterative, with feedback from later phases prompting earlier work.

Practice of creating graphic representations of quantitative and qualitative [[Data|data]] and [[Information|information]] using static, dynamic or interactive visual items. Data visualization presents mainly quantitative data in schematic form, using charts, graphs, geospatial maps, correlation matrices and percentage gauges. Information visualization handles large, complex datasets, including abstract information, with tools such as Sankey diagrams, [[Flowchart|flowcharts]] and timelines. Narrative visualization combines [[Data analysis|data analysis]], storytelling and visualization to reveal trends and relationships. Effective displays are well-sourced, uncluttered and accurate, and suit the expertise of their audience. The field draws on [[Statistics|statistics]], [[Graphic design|graphic design]], cognitive science and human-computer interaction. Because misleading graphics can spread misinformation, visualization literacy has become part of information literacy in the [[Information Age|information age]].

Building or room dedicated to housing computer equipment that stores, processes and transmits digital information. Uses include enterprise computing, [[Parallel computing|parallel computing]] for science and the military, web hosting, and training or running [[Artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence]] models. The early [[ENIAC]], completed in 1945, occupied entire rooms. Hyperscale [[Cloud computing|cloud]] facilities run by providers such as [[Amazon Web Services]] and [[Microsoft]] Azure can hold thousands of servers. In 2024, data centers used about 1.5% of global electricity, according to the International Energy Agency, and concerns over energy and water use have led to opposition to new facilities during the [[AI boom]].

Transfer of messages over a point-to-point or point-to-multipoint communication channel. It comprises transmission and reception and is classified as analog or digital. Analog systems convey voice, images or video as a continuous signal that varies in amplitude or phase, while digital transmission carries a digitized analog signal or a born-digital bitstream. Channels include copper wire, [[Optical fiber|optical fibers]], [[Radio wave|radio]] and [[Microwave|microwave]] links, [[Infrared|infrared]] signals and computer buses. Electrical telegraphy (1809) and teletypewriters (1906) were early digital applications. The theory is covered by [[Information theory|information theory]] and [[Coding theory|coding theory]], while courses address modulation and error-correcting codes at the physical layer and media access and error detection at the data link layer.

Encoding of [[Information|information]] using fewer [[Bit|bits]] than the original representation, to reduce file size. Lossless compression removes statistical redundancy so the original can be reconstructed exactly, with typical ratios of 2:1 to 4:1. Lossy compression discards less perceptible detail for higher ratios and is used for images, audio and video, as in [[JPEG]] and [[MP3]]. Techniques include run-length encoding, Huffman coding (David Huffman, 1952) and dictionary methods such as LZW, developed by Jacob Ziv and Abraham Lempel in 1977–1978 and used in ZIP and [[GIF]] files. The theory traces to [[Claude Shannon]], who established [[Entropy (information theory)|entropy]] as the theoretical minimum for lossless encoding.

Collection of discrete or continuous values that conveys quantity, quality, facts or statistics. A datum, or data point, is one individual value. Data is typically represented as numbers or characters and collected by measurement, [[Observation|observation]] or query. Raw data is usually cleaned before analysis by removing outliers and correcting errors. Examples include price indices, [[Unemployment|unemployment]] rates, [[Literacy|literacy]] rates and [[Census|census]] data. Thematically connected data in context can be viewed as [[Information|information]], and accumulated insight becomes [[Knowledge|knowledge]]. Big data, typically at the petabyte scale, is analyzed with [[Machine learning|machine learning]] methods in [[Data science|data science]]. Data has been described as "the new oil of the digital economy."

Interdisciplinary academic field that uses [[Statistics|statistics]], scientific computing, [[Scientific method|scientific methods]] and [[Algorithm|algorithms]] to extract knowledge from potentially noisy, structured or unstructured data. Data scientists write code in languages such as [[Python (programming language)|Python]], SQL and [[R (programming language)|R]], combining it with statistical knowledge to summarize data.

Recording of [[Information|information]] on a storage medium, such as handwriting, [[Magnetic tape|magnetic tape]] or [[Optical disc|optical discs]]. Recording may use virtually any form of [[Energy|energy]]. Biological molecules such as [[DNA]] and [[RNA]] are considered by some to be data storage. Data stored in a digital, machine-readable form is called digital data, and electronic storage requires electrical power. Computer storage is a core function of a general-purpose [[Computer|computer]]. Primary storage such as random access memory is volatile, while secondary storage, including hard disk drives, solid-state drives and optical media, retains data without power. [[Barcode|Barcodes]] and magnetic ink character recognition record machine-readable data on paper.

Way of organizing and storing data in a [[Computer|computer]] that is usually chosen for efficient access. In [[Computer science|computer science]], a data structure is the physical implementation of a data type, specifying data organization, storage format and the operations performed on it. Data structures are closely related to abstract data types, which describe the logical form or [[Algebraic structure|algebraic structure]] of a type without specifying how its operations are implemented. Linear structures such as arrays and linked lists arrange elements sequentially, while nonlinear structures such as trees and graphs support hierarchical or interconnected relationships. Choice involves trade-offs between storage space and speed, analyzed with measures such as Big-O notation.

Organized collection of [[Data|data]] in [[Computing|computing]], usually managed by a database management system (DBMS). The DBMS is the software that interacts with users, applications and the database to capture and analyze data, and it provides facilities to administer the database. The term is often used loosely for the DBMS, the wider database system or an associated application. Small databases may be kept on a [[File system|file system]], while large ones run on computer clusters or cloud storage. Relational databases, which store data in tables of rows and columns, became dominant in the 1980s, and most use [[SQL]] for writing and querying data. Non-relational databases, collectively called NoSQL, became popular in the 2000s and use different query languages.

Flowering palm (*Phoenix dactylifera*) of the family [[Arecaceae]], cultivated for its sweet fruit, the date. Native to a region from the Gulf states and [[Iraq]] to Pakistan and India, it is widely cultivated in [[North Africa]], the [[Middle East|Middle East]], Australia, South and Southeast Asia and [[Southern California]]. Date palms reach up to 30 m (98 ft) in height and can live more than 100 years. Dried dates contain 63–64% sugar by mass. Archaeological evidence of date cultivation in Arabia dates to the 6th millennium BCE, and the palm is described as emblematic of [[Oasis|oasis]] agriculture. It is also symbolic in Christian and Jewish religions.

Planned social encounters in which individuals get to know each other, often with a romantic or intimate purpose. Dating can lead to friendship, an [[Intimate relationship|intimate relationship]], [[Marriage|marriage]] or no relationship at all. Psychological studies find that it can foster personal growth through shared experiences and emotional exchange. It evolved from [[Courtship|courtship]] rituals aimed at family-vetted alliances, while contemporary forms emphasize individual choice and casual exploration. Online platforms have changed how people meet: about 10% of partnered U.S. adults met their current partner through a dating site or app as of 2023. Many encounters yield short-term outcomes rather than lasting partnerships.

Highly urbanized city (pop., 2024: 1,848,947), regional center of Davao Region, [[Philippines]]. At 2,443.61 sq km (943.48 sq mi), it is the largest city in the Philippines by land area. It is the third-most-populous city in the country after [[Quezon City]] and [[Manila]], and the most populous city in [[Mindanao]] and outside [[Metro Manila|Metro Manila]]. It is the center of Metro Davao, the second-most-populous metropolitan area in the country, and the main trade, commerce and industry hub of Mindanao. Mount Apo, the highest mountain in the Philippines, is highly visible from much of the city. The city is administered independently of Davao del Sur, the province in which it is geographically situated. It is nicknamed the Durian Capital of the Philippines.

American stand-up comedian, actor and former sketch comedian. He co-created and starred in the sketch series *Chappelle's Show* on Comedy Central, quitting midway through its third season. After returning to [[Stand-up comedy|stand-up]], he signed a $20-million-per-release comedy deal with [[Netflix]] in 2016. He has won six [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Awards]] for Best Comedy Album and twice won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series for hosting [[Saturday Night Live]].

Israelite king and second monarch of the united Kingdom of Israel, according to the [[Hebrew Bible]]. In the biblical narrative, David is a shepherd and harpist who kills the Philistine [[Goliath]] and later rules first Judah and then all Israel. He conquers [[Jerusalem]] and makes it his capital. His reign includes adultery with Bathsheba, the death of her husband, and a rebellion led by his son Absalom. Denied permission to build God's temple, he names [[Solomon]] as his successor. He is portrayed as an ideal king and ancestor of the future [[Messiah|Messiah]], and is referenced in the [[New Testament]]. The [[Quran|Quran]] and [[Hadith|hadith]] describe him as an Israelite king and a prophet. Most knowledge of David comes from biblical literature, whose historicity has been extensively challenged, and his reign may have occurred around the 9th century BC.

English broadcaster, naturalist and writer. His presenting career began with *Zoo Quest* in 1954 and spans seven decades, including *Planet Earth*, *The Blue Planet* and *Frozen Planet*. He held senior posts at the [[BBC]], including controller of BBC Two and director of programming for BBC Television, in the 1960s and 1970s. He is the only person to have won BAFTA Awards in black-and-white, color, high-definition, 3D and 4K, and he has won three Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Narrator. His later work has been increasingly vocal on environmental issues; he has advocated restoring [[Biodiversity|biodiversity]], limiting population growth, adopting [[Renewable energy|renewable energy]], mitigating [[Climate change|climate change]] and reducing meat consumption. NPR praised his "patented semi-whisper way of narrating."

English former footballer, primarily a right midfielder. Known for passing, crossing and set-piece taking, he won 19 major trophies and is the only English player to have won league titles in four countries. With [[Manchester|Manchester]] United he won six [[Premier League|Premier League]] titles and the [[UEFA Champions League]] in 1999. After four seasons at Real Madrid he moved to [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] LA Galaxy, with loan spells at [[AC Milan]] along the way. He captained England for six years and appeared at three [[FIFA World Cup|World Cups]]. He has been a [[UNICEF]] ambassador since 2005.

Primary national founder and first prime minister of [[Israel]], serving 1948–1963 apart from a break in 1954–55. As head of the Jewish Agency he led the movement for an independent Jewish state in [[Mandatory Palestine]]. On May 14, 1948, he proclaimed the establishment of Israel. Under his leadership Jewish militias were united into the [[Israel Defense Forces]] during the [[1948 Arab–Israeli War]], a war that also brought the flight or expulsion of most of the Palestinian Arab population. He improved relations with [[West Germany]] through a reparations agreement for Jewish property confiscated by the Nazis. He backed Israel's invasion of [[Egypt]] during the [[Suez Crisis]] in 1956. He retired in 1970 to Sde Boker, a [[Kibbutz|kibbutz]] in the Negev. [[Time (magazine)|Time]] magazine later named him one of the 100 most important people of the 20th century.

American [[Serial killer|serial killer]] and former U.S. Army soldier, also known as the Son of Sam. Between 1975 and 1977 he carried out a stabbing and a series of shootings in [[New York City]], killing six people and wounding 11. Arrested in August 1977 after a parking ticket proved a vital clue, he pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and received six concurrent life sentences. His crimes led to the Son of Sam laws in New York, which bar criminals from profiting from publicity about their crimes.

English singer, songwriter and actor, known for frequent reinvention. Regarded as one of the most influential musicians of the 20th century, he was often called the "chameleon of rock." His commercial breakthrough came in 1972 with the Ziggy Stardust persona and album during the glam rock era. The Berlin Trilogy, *Low*, *"Heroes"* and *Lodger*, moved him toward art rock, electronica and ambient music. His greatest commercial success came with *Let's Dance* (1983). Record sales were estimated at over 100 million, and he received six [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Awards]] and was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 1996. He was among the first artists to engage fans directly on the [[Internet|Internet]], through his BowieNet website. His last album, *Blackstar*, was released two days before his death.

British [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] politician, prime minister of the United Kingdom (2010–2016). He led the party from 2005 to 2016 and headed a coalition with the Liberal Democrats after 2010. His premiership was shaped by the [[2008 financial crisis|2008 financial crisis]] and the [[Great Recession|Great Recession]]; critics have faulted its austerity measures, while supporters credit him with modernizing the party and reducing the deficit. His government legalized [[Same-sex marriage|same-sex marriage]] in England and Wales. He introduced the [[Brexit|Brexit referendum]] in 2016 and resigned as prime minister after the Vote Leave campaign won.

American actor and director, known for the television series *Kung Fu* (1972–1975). He played Kwai Chang Caine, a Shaolin monk, in the series, and portrayed [[Woody Guthrie]] in *Bound for Glory* (1976). He appeared in [[Martin Scorsese]]'s *Boxcar Bertha* (1972). His career resurged as Bill in [[Quentin Tarantino]]'s *Kill Bill* films (2003–2004), which won him a Saturn Award. He received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame|Hollywood Walk of Fame]] in 1997. He was found dead in a [[Bangkok|Bangkok]] hotel room; the cause was ruled accidental.

Canadian film director, screenwriter and producer, a principal originator of body horror. Dubbed "Canada's King of Horror," he makes [[Science fiction|science fiction]] horror films that explore bodily transformation, infectious disease and the intertwining of psychological and technological themes, including *Shivers* (1975), *Videodrome* (1983) and *The Fly* (1986). *Crash* won the Special Jury Prize at the [[Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] in 1996. Seven of his films have competed for the Palme d'Or, and he collaborated with Viggo Mortensen on *A History of Violence* (2005) and *Eastern Promises* (2007).
